chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, by his chain, raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no one among the children of Adam except that he has two veins: a vein in his head that incites leprosy, and a vein in his body that incites vitiligo. So when the vein in the head becomes active, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends catarrh upon it until what is in it of the disease flows out. And when the vein in the body becomes active, Allah sends warts upon it until what is in it of the disease flows out. So when one of you sees catarrh and warts, let him praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for the health.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Catarrh is excess in the head.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of having a runny nose or warts according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (as) elucidates the prophetic tradition that minor ailments like catarrh and warts serve as divine mechanisms for purging excess humors and diseases from the body's specific veins. It encourages believers to perceive these transient discomforts not as burdens, but as signs of Allah’s mercy in preserving overall health by expelling internal corruption. This perspective aligns with the Shia understanding of 'affiya' (well-being) as a state where the body is actively cleansing itself, reflecting the balance between physical physiology and spiritual gratitude.
